boards.title: Your First Weekend at Lafayette College, Shared as Cards
boards.description: A Friday-to-Sunday sequence connecting campus essentials, student programming, art, downtown Easton, recreation, and Lafayette’s working farm.

cards.title: Friday Arrival: Find Markle Hall
cards.subtitle: Start with a campus-map anchor
cards.notes: Locate Markle Hall on the official map, then use it as your first waypoint while learning the paths across College Hill.
cards.short_summary: Begin with a clearly mapped administrative landmark before exploring farther.
cards.evidence_claim: Lafayette College’s official campus map identifies Markle Hall as a named campus destination.
cards.access_notes: Use the official campus map for navigation; building access may depend on College operations.

cards.title: Friday Dinner at Upper Farinon
cards.subtitle: Settle in with an on-campus meal
cards.notes: Check the live dining page before leaving your residence, then meet your group inside Farinon for an easy first dinner.
cards.short_summary: Use a central campus dining hall as the weekend’s first shared meal stop.
cards.evidence_claim: Lafayette Dining lists Upper Farinon Dining Hall and standard academic-year hours of 8 a.m.–9 p.m. Monday through Saturday.
cards.access_notes: Standard academic-year Friday and Saturday hours are 8 a.m.–9 p.m.; verify live hours before visiting.

cards.title: Friday Night at The Spot
cards.subtitle: Join a campus-programmed late-night event
cards.notes: Check the announced program, bring your Lafayette ID, and use the campus shuttle if it is running for that evening’s event.
cards.short_summary: Close Friday at Lafayette’s student-focused weekend programming venue.
cards.evidence_claim: During fall and spring semesters, Student Life programs weekend events at The Spot from 9 p.m. as late as 2 a.m.; access is limited to Lafayette affiliates and their guests.
cards.source_title: The Spot | Lafayette's Late Night Destination
cards.access_notes: Weekend programs may run 9 p.m.–2 a.m. while College is in session. Lafayette students, faculty, staff, and permitted guests only.

cards.title: Saturday Reset at Skillman Library
cards.subtitle: Orient yourself to the main library
cards.notes: Walk through Skillman, identify the service points you will need later, and confirm that day’s posted hours before arriving.
cards.short_summary: Turn a quiet Saturday visit into practical library orientation.
cards.evidence_claim: Lafayette College Libraries identifies Skillman Library as a campus library and publishes its current daily hours online.
cards.access_notes: Daily hours vary by term and date; consult the library’s current schedule before visiting.

cards.title: Saturday Art at Williams Center Gallery
cards.subtitle: See a free campus exhibition
cards.notes: Enter through the Williams Center for the Arts, view the current exhibition, and allow time to read the gallery labels.
cards.short_summary: Add a no-cost contemporary and historical art stop to Saturday afternoon.
cards.evidence_claim: Lafayette states that its gallery exhibitions and related programs are free and open to the public; Williams Center Gallery is open Wednesday–Sunday, noon–5 p.m.
cards.access_notes: Open Wednesday–Sunday, noon–5 p.m.; closed during holidays and campus closures.

cards.title: Follow the Karl Stirner Arts Trail
cards.subtitle: Walk beside Bushkill Creek toward downtown
cards.notes: Wear walking shoes, stay on the established trail, and photograph the public artworks without climbing on installations.
cards.short_summary: Connect campus and downtown through a creekside corridor of outdoor art.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Easton describes the Karl Stirner Arts Trail as a 1.75-mile route along Bushkill Creek within walking distance of Lafayette College and downtown.
cards.source_title: Karl Stirner Arts Trail | Easton, PA
cards.access_notes: Outdoor conditions and daylight vary; use the established trail and check local notices before setting out.

cards.title: Browse Easton Public Market
cards.subtitle: Pause downtown for food and local vendors
cards.notes: Walk through the vendor floor first, compare available options, and check individual vendor hours before ordering anything.
cards.short_summary: Use the indoor market as a flexible downtown meal and browsing stop.
cards.evidence_claim: Easton Public Market is a year-round indoor market at 325 Northampton Street with food vendors, a farm stand, demonstration kitchen, and community room.
cards.access_notes: Market hours are Friday–Saturday 9 a.m.–8 p.m. and Sunday 9 a.m.–5 p.m.; individual vendor hours may vary.

cards.title: Stop at the Lafayette College Store
cards.subtitle: Learn where course and campus supplies are sold
cards.notes: Find the store on the official map, note its location for future errands, and verify operating hours before heading over.
cards.short_summary: Add a practical campus-supplies waypoint before returning uphill.
cards.evidence_claim: Lafayette College’s official campus map identifies the Lafayette College Store as a named campus destination.
cards.access_notes: Retail hours are not established by the cited map; check the store’s current schedule before visiting.

cards.title: Sunday Movement at Kirby Sports Center
cards.subtitle: Try an easy recreation-center session
cards.notes: Bring your Lafayette ID, choose a familiar low-risk workout, and arrive at least 20 minutes before the entry doors lock.
cards.short_summary: Start Sunday with a straightforward introduction to campus recreation.
cards.evidence_claim: Lafayette Recreation Services operates at Kirby Sports Center and requires patrons to present a valid Lafayette ID or Facility Access Pass.
cards.source_title: Hours of Operation · Recreation Services · Lafayette College
cards.access_notes: Regular semester weekend hours are 10 a.m.–10 p.m.; doors lock 20 minutes before closing. Break and special-event schedules vary.

cards.title: Finish Sunday at LaFarm
cards.subtitle: See Lafayette’s working farm and community garden
cards.notes: Arrange the campus shuttle, a bike, or a carpool in advance, then contact LaFarm before planning any hands-on participation.
cards.short_summary: End the sequence by connecting campus dining with Lafayette’s food-growing work.
cards.evidence_claim: LaFarm is Lafayette’s three-acre working farm and community garden beside Metzgar Fields, three miles north of campus, with production fields, pollinator gardens, tunnels, and a greenhouse.
cards.access_notes: Located three miles north of campus; Lafayette recommends biking, carpooling, or using the campus shuttle. Contact staff before participating.
